newsitem.title: CHILE: Four die in Chilean copper mine tunnel collapse.
newsitem.headline: Four die in Chilean copper mine tunnel collapse.

text.p: Four Chilean copper miners died on Wednesday when an earth-covered tunnel collapsed beneath them, burying them under tons of earth and rock in the third fatal mining accident in Chile this week, the mine's owners said.
Workers at the El Abra copper mine in arid northern Chile were loading earth on top of a covering over a conveyor belt when the covering's steel structure suddenly collapsed, El Abra officials said.
Four workers were buried beneath the debris and their bodies were recovered hours later, spokesmen said.
Officials originally spoke of a rockslide but clarified later the circumstances of the accident at El Abra, lying in the Atacama desert about 900 miles (1500 km) north of Santiago.
"The collapse of the structure completely trapped the four workers. As a consequence of the accident, they died," said El Abra in a statement.

Copper production at the mine was paralyzed. Owned by Englewood, Colorado-based Cyprus Amax Minerals and Chilean state firm Codelco, the mine came on stream in August and was due to move into full production next year as one of Chile's largest mines.
Officials had no word yet whether those plans would be delayed.
"Obviously we have been worried about other things today ... We've had 100 percent of staff dedicated to the rescue efforts," said the mine's human resources manager, Rodrigo Salinas.

The accident buried about 300 yards (300 meters) of a conveyor belt which carries the mine's copper ore to a crusher plant and forms the mine's lifeline. Normal production could not resume until workers uncovered the belt, officials said.
The accident added to an unusual rash of mining accidents in Chile this week.

On Sunday, a worker died at Codelco's El Teniente mine when he tumbled down a 19-yard (19-meter) pit, and another miner died at Codelco's Andina mine two days later when he was hit in the head by a swinging steel door. Production was not affected in either of those accidents.
